subject: 2–3 a.m.
fact: The time Sylvira Savikas was seen glowing red in candlelight and carrying a lantern — a critical anomaly given her tiefling physiology — suggesting deliberate illumination of a scene or object at the moment of or after the murder.
source_quote: I swear I could see that devil woman's — Sylvira Savikas's — face glowing red in the candlelight… around 2 or 3 in the morning.

subject: Dead Winter
fact: The gift tag references 'a proper Dead Winter gift' — indicating the murder occurred during or shortly after the seasonal observance known as Dead Winter.
source_quote: *To Janussi... a proper Dead Winter gift...*

subject: Deadwinter Day
fact: Deadwinter Day is the upcoming event during which Janussi was preparing to clear business — marking the temporal context of his final meetings and the urgency of his actions before his death.
source_quote: clearing business before Deadwinter Day.

subject: Deadwinter Day
fact: Janussi was preparing for Deadwinter Day, holding final meetings with Great Readers; the murder occurred just before this ceremonial deadline, suggesting the crime was timed to disrupt a ritual, transfer of power, or archive opening.

subject: elapsed time
fact: An hour passes between Janussi’s dinner and his death, during which his nose was broken and he was assaulted.
source_quote: Within the evening — Janussi had eaten dinner with his face intact and his teeth whole. Whatever happened, happened in the narrow window between that meal and his death.

subject: elapsed time
fact: An hour passes between two events in the session.
source_quote: An hour later

subject: elapsed time
fact: The investigation spans months of tension and overlapping patterns between Thorin and Grygum, indicating the grudge between Daral and Janussi has been developing for years, and the murder is the culmination of a long-brewing conflict.
source_quote: months in a tunnel will teach two people to think along the same line...

subject: elapsed time
fact: Thirty minutes passed between the disturbance and Queenie's awakening by Sylvira Savikas.
source_quote: only to be rudely awakened some thirty minutes later by our Sylvira Savikas

subject: evening of the incident
fact: The events unfolded on an evening following supper, with Queenie observing Daral's departure around eight, and the shapeshifter appearing during the nighttime cycle.
source_quote: She woke from her afternoon nap around eight, after supper... she'd prowled the nighttime cycle...

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493 DR.
source_quote: On the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the day Janussi, Keeper of the Tome, was found dead with his heart torn out and blackened finger and lip stains.
source_quote: There is a particular comfort in a corpse. It does not lie. It does not run a counter-play. Everything it knows is written on it, and all I have to do is read.

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the morning after supper, when Queenie awoke from her afternoon nap around eight.
source_quote: She woke from her afternoon nap around eight, after supper

subject: Time of Attack
fact: Sylvira attacked Janussi approximately thirty minutes before Queenie’s afternoon nap, placing the event in the morning.
source_quote: some thirty minutes later by our Sylvira Savikas, this is in the morning

subject: Time of Daral’s Exit
fact: Daral exited the tower after supper, around eight in the evening, while Janussi was still alive.
source_quote: She woke from her afternoon nap around eight, after supper

subject: time of death
fact: Grygum died sometime after an assault (broken nose with settled bruising) and before the heart extraction. The poison was ingested while reading, suggesting death occurred hours after dinner — likely in the evening. The lack of forced entry and the presence of tobacco smoke imply the killer arrived during normal hours, possibly as a visitor.
source_quote: Somewhere between dinner and the moment his heart was carved out, someone had struck this man in the face hard enough to break the bone.

subject: time of death
fact: Janussi was assaulted and poisoned between dinner and his death, with the final act occurring within the same evening — the broken nose and tooth chip occurred before the heart was removed, and the ink on *The Discoveries* was the last thing written before death.
source_quote: Within the evening — Janussi had eaten dinner with his face intact and his teeth whole.

subject: Book Removal and Deletion
fact: Daral removed *The Golden Ass* from the Hightower Library and activated it, causing its contents to be deleted. The book's removal coincided with Janussi’s final moments and suggests a deliberate attempt to erase evidence.
source_quote: that stuff got deleted off that book that no one should have touched.

subject: broken nose
fact: Janussi’s nose was broken before death, as evidenced by bruising that cannot form on a corpse, placing the injury within the final moments of his life, prior to the heart removal.
source_quote: Bruising doesn't form on a corpse; there's no living tissue to swell.

subject: daral's departure
fact: Daral exited with 'The Golden Ass' while the victim was still alive.
source_quote: Daral exited with the book, and the dead man was not yet dead.

subject: Daral’s Exit
fact: Daral exited the tower while Janussi was still alive, carrying *The Golden Ass*. This establishes a clear timeline: Janussi was murdered after Daral left.
source_quote: the victim was still alive when Daral left

subject: Daral's second visit
fact: Daral Yashenti returned to Janussi’s chamber at half past ten, drunk, pounded on the door, argued loudly, and then fled down the stairs — the first time Janussi was seen running away from someone.
source_quote: Daral came back at half past ten, drunk as a skunk, pounding on the door until Janussi let him in, another loud argument, then the slam and the great reader running back down the stairs.

subject: dart impacts on armchair
fact: Three circular impacts and holes in the armchair suggest a magical dart weapon was fired at the chair — not the Keeper — indicating an outburst of rage directed at an object, not a person.
source_quote: Three circular impacts, horsehair stuffing scattered, two holes punched clean through the chair back. Daz's mind clicked again — material components, every pouch a spell — and he murmured, 'a little bit of this, a little bit of that,' pleased with himself. But one sapphire was missing. One parchment. 'Somebody is trying to build a sapphire spell,' he said, 'a spell that requires a sapphire.'

subject: Daz
fact: Daz notices that the phrase 'hypnotic block' is doing work the describer doesn't understand.
source_quote: Something in the phrasing snagged. I have spent my life learning to notice when a description is doing work the describer doesn't understand.

subject: Daz's cat interrogation
fact: Daz used a Stonespeaker crystal to communicate with the five-year-old housecat in the murder chamber.
source_quote: I think I can talk to the cat... It's part of what the stone speaker crystal grants me.

subject: daz's final tickle offer
fact: Daz offered more tickles and padding to settle the account fully.
source_quote: More tickles, more padding," I offered, because the account wasn't quite settled.

subject: daz's tickle
fact: Daz gave Queenie a little tickle, which prompted her to deliver critical information.
source_quote: I'll give Queenie a little tickle," I said, and tickled.

subject: desecration of Janussi's body
fact: Janussi's heart was torn out and ribcage smashed with precise, deliberate strokes after death, indicating the killer was not trying to kill but to desecrate the corpse at leisure.
source_quote: The heart was gone — torn out, not for any wound it would cause, but as a guard against any working that calls the dead back to answer.

subject: discovery of Janussi's body
fact: Janussi’s body was found at dawn by A'lai Aivenmore, the Great Reader, who knocked over the statue in shock — the statue had simply fallen, not been moved deliberately.
source_quote: The statue had simply fallen, it turned out. The Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore had knocked it over in shock when he found the body at dawn.

subject: force-dart impacts on armchair
fact: Three circular punctures in the armchair back and scattered horsehair; darts of pure force fired with intent but missed the target — suggesting an emotional outburst directed at the chair, not the victim.
source_quote: Somebody had been furious. But not at the keeper — those darts never miss their mark, and the man bore no such marks.

subject: Glabbagool's failed analysis
fact: Glabbagool, an ooze that has consumed the Underdark, could not identify the black substance on Janussi’s body, confirming it was an unknown and exceptionally dangerous material.
source_quote: We gave him the substance. He gave it his best. It wasn't enough — a thin first effort, then a second pass with help, and still nothing he could name. But even his failure carried a verdict: there was *something* about the black, something that mattered. When even a creature that has eaten the Underdark can't place a poison, you've learned the poison is worth being afraid of.

subject: Great Readers' meetings
fact: Multiple explosive meetings occurred between Janussi and the Great Readers in the hours before his death, with at least half ending in shouting matches and personal accusations.
source_quote: Janussi had spent his last morning in a series of one-on-one meetings with the Great Readers… at least half of them… had ended in explosive shouting matches.

subject: grygum's expense reduction
fact: Someone else had taken an expense off Grygum's account, relieving him.
source_quote: someone else had just taken an expense off his account

subject: impersonation of Sylvira Savikas
fact: A figure wearing Sylvira Savikas’s appearance but lacking her scent was observed descending the tower steps, indicating the presence of a shapeshifter.
source_quote: But she didn't smell like the demon lady, though.

subject: Janussi's death sequence
fact: Janussi was assaulted before death — struck in the face, breaking his nose — then returned to his desk, wrote in *The Discoveries*, read a poisoned page, wetted his fingertip on his lip, fell forward, chipping his tooth, and was later found and desecrated by a deliberate, unhurried killer who removed his heart and took one sapphire and a locket.
source_quote: A man at his books, wetting his finger to turn a poisoned page. The black climbing through him while he read on, suspecting nothing. A fall, forward, hard — a broken nose, a chipped tooth on the stone. And then the patient hands arriving after, in no hurry at all, rolling the body and opening the chest to make certain he stayed gone.

subject: Janussi's final act
fact: Janussi was writing in blue ink on 'The Discoveries' moments before his death, smudging his finger and lip with poisoned ink.
source_quote: The blue ink on 'The Discoveries' had been laid down after the blue ink on another book. 'The Golden Ass.' 'So that's the last thing he was writing?' Confirmation. The spell research was the final thing under his hand.

subject: Janussi's final meetings
fact: Janussi held a series of one-on-one meetings with the Great Readers the morning of his death, each ending in explosive shouting matches with Kalan, Teles, Daral, and Sylvira.
source_quote: Janussi had spent his last morning in a series of one-on-one meetings with the Great Readers, clearing business before Deadwinter Day.

subject: Janussi's final night
fact: A thud was heard at midnight, followed by the appearance of Sylvira Savikas carrying a lantern she had no need for.
source_quote: I heard a thud upstairs... I swear I could see that devil woman's face glowing red in the candlelight... she was carrying a lantern.

subject: Janussi's murder
fact: Janussi was murdered under circumstances suggesting an insider attack — the locket around his neck is missing, and the book he was studying was deleted or removed, pointing to a targeted act of theft or sabotage tied to the Hightower Library’s secrets.
source_quote: The locket was missing. Off Janussi's neck... that book that no one should have touched.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch's confrontation
fact: Kalan Strongbranch had a face like thunder when encountered by Hollypocket on the steps.
source_quote: I passed Kalan Strongbranch on the steps. He had a face like thunder, nearly knocked the tray out of my hands.

subject: keeper's death
fact: Grygum was killed after being assaulted — his nose broken, his body poisoned by reading a cursed book, and his heart carved out post-mortem. The killer rolled his body over after death, suggesting a ritual or concealment. The poisoning was slow, allowing time for the assault and struggle. The killer did not force entry and took only one sapphire and one parchment, leaving behind a treasury.
source_quote: Whoever did this came in, took one sapphire, and walked past a king's ransom.

subject: loot selection
fact: The killer took only one sapphire and one spell parchment from the safe — leaving behind a small treasury — indicating the theft was targeted for a specific spell, not greed.
source_quote: Whoever did this came in, took one sapphire, and walked past a king's ransom. 'I mean, well, that can eliminate some former adventurers,' I said. The greedy don't leave the gold. This was a man who needed exactly one thing.

subject: Lover's Quarrel with Force
fact: Sylvira Savikas attacked Janussi with a lance of force during a romantic dispute, waking Queenie from her nap. This event initiated the chain of disturbances leading to Janussi’s death.
source_quote: blasting the armchamber with a lance of unerring force light.

subject: midnight thud
fact: A thud was heard upstairs shortly after midnight, following the bell tower's chime, and was the last confirmed sound of Janussi being alive — interpreted by Hollypocket as the moment his life ended.
source_quote: I thought I heard a thud upstairs… I never slept before eleven… that was how she knew he had been alive until the thud.

subject: midnight thud
fact: The midnight thud is reported by Hollypocket as a sound heard upstairs after the bell tower rang, which she later realized may have been the moment Janussi died.
source_quote: I thought I heard a thud upstairs.

subject: murder of Janussi
fact: Janussi was assaulted (broken nose), poisoned (black substance ingested while reading), fell forward (chipped tooth), and was then murdered (heart removed, body repositioned) — all in a sequence spanning minutes to hours, with the killer returning after death to desecrate the body.
source_quote: Died on his face. Got turned over by his killer. The sequence had a horrible tidiness to it.

subject: murder of Janussi
fact: Janussi was murdered likely by poison, with the scent masked by his habitual tobacco smoke; the crime occurred after midnight, following a series of hostile encounters with colleagues; the missing comedy book and locket suggest a theft tied to a cipher or hidden knowledge.

subject: queenie's breath-holding habit
fact: Queenie holds her breath whenever a two-legger passes, judging them unclean.
source_quote: I try to hold my breath whenever a two-legger passes. It's clear that you hardly ever lick yourselves at all.

subject: queenie's final dismissal
fact: Queenie dismissed the party with the instruction to lick themselves before returning.
source_quote: You may now leave, and please give yourself a proper licking before returning to my tower.

subject: sequence of death
fact: Janussi was assaulted (broken nose), returned to his desk to write, ingested poison via ink-stained finger, fell face-first (chipped tooth), and was then murdered (heart removed, body rolled) by a deliberate, unhurried killer.
source_quote: A man at his books, wetting his finger to turn a poisoned page. The black climbing through him while he read on, suspecting nothing. A fall, forward, hard — a broken nose, a chipped tooth on the stone. And then the patient hands arriving after, in no hurry at all, rolling the body and opening the chest to make certain he stayed gone.

subject: shapeshifter encounter
fact: A figure wearing Sylvira's shape but none of her scent appeared — a shapeshifter impersonation.
source_quote: But she didn't smell like the demon lady, though. A figure wearing Sylvira and none of her scent.

subject: statue fall
fact: The statue of the Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore was knocked over accidentally by shock upon discovering the body — not by magic or sabotage.
source_quote: The statue had simply fallen, it turned out. The Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore had knocked it over in shock when he found the body at dawn.

subject: sylvira's attack
fact: Sylvira Savikas blasted the armchamber with a lance of unerring force light, waking Queenie.
source_quote: blasting the armchamber with a lance of unerring force light

subject: Sylvira Savikas's midnight visit
fact: Sylvira Savikas, a tiefling who sees in darkness, was seen carrying a lantern at 2–3 AM, glowing red in candlelight.
source_quote: she was carrying a lantern. She's a tiefling, and she can see in the dark without any light at all.

subject: Sylvira's nocturnal appearance
fact: Sylvira Savikas was seen by Hollypocket at 2–3 a.m. with her face glowing red in candlelight, carrying a lantern she had no need for, then vanishing.
source_quote: I swear I could see that devil woman's — Sylvira Savikas's — face glowing red in the candlelight.

subject: Teles Ahvoste's accusation
fact: Teles Ahvoste shouted 'hypocrite' at Janussi during a heated meeting.
source_quote: I did hear Teles shout, *hypocrite*, at poor Janussi before he stormed out.

subject: the attack on the armchair
fact: Three darts of pure force were fired at the armchair in the Keeper's Chamber, missing Janussi entirely, suggesting the attacker was enraged but not targeting the Keeper directly at that moment.
source_quote: Three circular impacts, horsehair stuffing scattered, two holes punched clean through the chair back. He studied it and pronounced it: darts of pure force. Somebody had been furious. But not at the keeper — those darts never miss their mark, Thorin pointed out, and the man bore no such marks. Somebody had aimed three bolts of force at a chair.

subject: the cipher theory
fact: The cipher theory is proposed by Thorin — that Janussi used *The Golden Ass* as a key to a replacement cipher, and the book’s absence prevents decryption.
source_quote: There's something written in the book that wasn't part of the original book — or maybe he's using the book and the notes to do some sort of cipher.

subject: the discovery of the body
fact: The Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore discovered the body at dawn and knocked over the marble statue of himself in shock, an accidental disruption to the scene.
source_quote: The statue had simply fallen, it turned out. The Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore had knocked it over in shock when he found the body at dawn.

subject: theft of *The Golden Ass*
fact: *The Golden Ass*, a dull book capable of rendering observers motionless and uninterested, was removed from the Hightower Library by Daral. Its removal coincided with the erasure of records and preceded Janussi's death.
source_quote: Every time they open that block, they just sit there and don't tickle!

subject: the interrogation of the statue
fact: Thorin expressed fear that the statue of the Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore might awaken, causing Tadric to become unnerved, though the statue had merely been knocked over accidentally.
source_quote: 'Shake the candle,' Thorin said. 'I don't want it to wake up and attack us,' Thorin explained. 'I've had, you know, had bad experiences.' It worked on poor Tadric exactly as you'd fear. He tried not to look at the candle and then could not stop looking at the candle, and finally turned to Thorin. 'Are you sure this — is it true about candles?'

subject: the missing book
fact: The missing book — *The Golden Ass* — is described as having been annotated by Janussi with jokes and spell notes, then walked out of the room, and is suspected of containing a cipher or replacement code.
source_quote: The Golden Ass was a comedy. Janussi had been writing down jokes he found funny — the man had a sense of humor he'd evidently kept private.

subject: the poison theory
fact: The poison theory is proposed as the reason the smoke in Janussi’s chamber was used — not to kill, but to mask the smell of poison, and the black residue on his mouth supports this.
source_quote: The one thing that tobacco smoke would do is hide the smell of poison.

subject: the theft from the safe
fact: The safe was opened without force, and only one sapphire and one parchment were taken, while a vast treasure remained untouched, indicating the thief had a precise, non-greedy objective.
source_quote: The killer had the combination, or had no need of one. In other words, score what they left them. A small fortune, untouched. Whoever did this came in, took one sapphire, and walked past a king's ransom.

subject: thorin's force bolt inquiry
fact: Thorin questioned why the bolts of force were being used — prompting the revelation of Sylvira’s attack.
source_quote: what was going on with those bolts of force, do we know why

subject: travel to Sloobludop
fact: Sloobludop is approximately eight days away via the Darklake.
source_quote: the town of Sloopdopblop is just eight days away

subject: travel to Sloobludop
fact: The town of Sloopdopblop is just eight days away via the Darklake.
source_quote: the town of Sloopdopblop is just eight days away

subject: zalthir's tv deduction
fact: Zalthir declared 'Oh, it's a TV!' — a misidentification that nonetheless arrived at the correct functional conclusion.
source_quote: Oh, it's a TV!" said Zalthir, which was not quite the deduction but arrived at the same destination.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is an institution of scholarly preservation, but its culture is poisoned by entrenched grudges, silent rivalries, and the slow accumulation of grievances — a contrast to the overt violence of the Underdark, where deception is honest and immediate.
source_quote: I despise this whole place a little — not Candlekeep, Candlekeep's fine, the books are fine — but the *culture* of it, the scholars who keep grudges the way a dragon keeps gold...

subject: Candlekeep Scribes
fact: The use of midnight blue ink — the ink used in Candlekeep’s books — confirms Janussi was engaged in official transcription work, implicating the Archive’s internal practices or texts as potential sources of the threat.
source_quote: Wasn't the blue ink — the ink they used in the books?

subject: Great Readers
fact: The Great Readers are a scholarly faction within the Keeper's tower, known for intense intellectual disputes, with at least five members having had violent confrontations with Janussi in the hours before his death.
source_quote: That was the thing about a place full of scholars — they would shed blood over a marginal note and call it discourse.

subject: Hightower Library
fact: The Hightower Library is a restricted location with two physical keys — one held by Janussi, the other by Kalan. It is associated with a missing book, *The Golden Ass*, and records that were erased or deleted.
source_quote: Someone snuck in. That might explain why that stuff got deleted off that book that no one should have touched.

subject: Hightower Library
fact: The Hightower Library is a restricted repository containing volumes that may not be touched without authorization. A book — *The Golden Ass* — was removed from it, and its contents were deleted, suggesting a deliberate act of sabotage or concealment tied to the keys held by Janussi and Kalan.
source_quote: that stuff got deleted off that book that no one should have touched.

subject: Hightower Library
fact: The Hightower Library is secured by two keys — one held by the deceased Janussi, the other by gate warden Kalan Strongbranch; access to its archives is tightly controlled, and unauthorized tampering may have motivated the murder.

subject: The Garden Shadow
fact: The Garden Shadow is an organization or group known for the aphorism that a room reveals itself most through what is missing — a principle referenced by the narrator as influential despite not being directly attributed to any single member.
source_quote: The Garden Shadow had a saying about that — or possibly Brother Tharusk did... The point survived anyway: count what should be present before you count what is.

subject: The Keepers of Candlekeep
fact: The Keepers maintained a secure, magically protected archive; Janussi’s role as Keeper implied access to rare and dangerous knowledge; the presence of sealed spell pouches and rare components suggests the institution was a center for advanced arcane research.
source_quote: Material components, every pouch a spell — and he murmured, 'a little bit of this, a little bit of that.'

subject: unknown cult or arcane order
fact: The precision of the theft — taking only one sapphire and one spell parchment while ignoring vast wealth, the use of poison via a cursed book, the removal of a sacred chain, and the symbolic destruction of the statue — suggests a ritualistic faction or secretive arcane order. The killer acted with knowledge of the keeper’s work, access to the safe, and intent to complete a specific spell, not to plunder.
source_quote: This was a man who needed exactly one thing.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is referenced as a place with fine books but a toxic culture of scholars who hoard grudges like dragons hoard gold.
source_quote: I despise this whole place a little — not Candlekeep, Candlekeep's fine, the books are fine — but the *culture* of it

subject: corridor
fact: Queenie retreated to the corridor after Daral shouted too much, and later saw him run downstairs with a hypnotic block.
source_quote: she retreated to the corridor — "when I later saw him run downstairs with a hypnotic block."

subject: corridor retreat
fact: Queenie retreated to the corridor when Daral ran downstairs with the hypnotic block.
source_quote: she retreated to the corridor — 'when I later saw him run downstairs with a hypnotic block.'

subject: crime scene — Keeper’s chamber
fact: The crime scene contained a chipped tooth on the floor near the body, indicating Janussi fell face-first before death, and his body was later rolled onto his back by the killer.
source_quote: He had fallen forward. Face-first. Chipped the tooth on the way down. And then someone had come in, after, and rolled him onto his back to take the heart.

subject: Garden Shadow
fact: The Garden Shadow is referenced as having a saying about absence — 'a room tells you most by what it is missing' — though it is unclear whether the saying belongs to the place or to Brother Tharusk.
source_quote: The Garden Shadow had a saying about that — or possibly Brother Tharusk did, the tall one who always smelled of incense

subject: Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore statue
fact: The three-foot marble statue of the Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore was knocked over by shock upon discovering the body — not by sabotage, but by an accidental collision.
source_quote: The statue had simply fallen, it turned out. The Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore had knocked it over in shock when he found the body at dawn.

subject: Hightower Library
fact: The Hightower Library is a restricted archive containing forbidden or volatile texts. *The Golden Ass* was stolen from here, and its deletion suggests the library’s protections were bypassed or corrupted.
source_quote: that book that no one should have touched

subject: Hightower Library
fact: The Hightower Library is a restricted archive within Candlekeep, housing forbidden or sensitive texts; its dual-key security system implies high-level access control, and the deletion of content indicates a breach by someone with access to one or both keys.
source_quote: Janussi held one of the two keys of the Hightower Library.

subject: Hightower Library
fact: The Hightower Library is referenced as having two keys — one held by the dead Janussi and one held by the gate warden Kalan — and is implied to have had materials deleted or tampered with.
source_quote: Janussi held one of the two keys of the, of the Hightower Library.

subject: Hightower Library key location
fact: One key to the Hightower Library was held by Janussi; the other is held by the gate warden, Kalan.
source_quote: Fembris... supplied the column I was missing: Janussi held one of the two keys to the Hightower Library. The other key... rested with Kalan, the gate warden.

subject: Hollypocket's apartment location
fact: Hollypocket's apartment is located below the Keeper's tower, modest but warm.
source_quote: Hollypocket's apartment sat below the Keeper's tower — modest, but with room to breathe, and warm.

subject: Janussi's armchair
fact: Janussi's armchair is where Queenie had settled for a nap, only to be rudely awakened thirty minutes later by Sylvira Savikas blasting the armchamber with a lance of unerring force light.
source_quote: She had settled into Janussi's armchair for a nap, she said, "only to be rudely awakened some thirty minutes later by our Sylvira Savikas, this is in the morning, blasting the armchamber with a lance of unerring force light."

subject: janussi's armchair
fact: Queenie had settled into Janussi's armchair for a nap before being awakened.
source_quote: She had settled into Janussi's armchair for a nap

subject: Janussi's chamber
fact: Janussi's chamber contained a comedy book annotated with spell notes and jokes in the same ink, a tobacco-stained atmosphere, a missing locket, and signs of a struggle; the book was later observed to have walked out of the room — a metaphor for its physical disappearance.

subject: Keeper's Chamber
fact: A three-foot marble statue of the hooded bearded old man holding a candle aloft — the Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore — was toppled near the armchairs and tea table, having been knocked over in shock upon discovering the body.
source_quote: Last, the statue. Three feet of marble, a hooded bearded old man holding a candle aloft, toppled on the floor near the armchairs and the tea table. The statue had simply fallen, it turned out. The Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore had knocked it over in shock when he found the body at dawn.

subject: Keeper's Chamber
fact: The Keeper's Chamber contained a desk with *The Discoveries* and *The Golden Ass*, blue ink, a wastebasket with a gift tag, tobacco smoke residue, black residue on Janussi’s mouth and fingers, and a marble statue that had been knocked over — the only item missing was *The Golden Ass*.
source_quote: The only thing gone. A room tells you most by what it is missing.

subject: Keeper's Chamber
fact: The Keeper's Chamber contained a silver pedestal, an ebony pipe with cherry tobacco, an open safe with scattered empty pouches, loose sapphires, and scraps of parchment naming spells, with four sealed pouches, a figurine of a raven, a potion of supreme healing, a potion of water breathing, five diamonds, platinum, and gold left untouched.
source_quote: The safe. A box of metal as wide as a man's reach, sunk into the tower wall, its door standing open. Empty pouches scattered in front of it, sapphires loose and dazzling, scraps of parchment naming spells. But still inside the safe were four sealed pouches, each with its sapphire — and beside them a figurine of a raven, a potion of supreme healing, another of water breathing, five diamonds each worth a fortune, a heap of platinum and gold, a small treasury left untouched.

subject: Keeper's Chamber
fact: The Keeper's Chamber held an armchair with three circular impacts and two holes punched clean through the back, indicating darts of pure force had been fired at it, not at the body.
source_quote: Daz drifted to the armchair next, and read the wounds in it the way he'd read the wounds in the man. Three circular impacts, horsehair stuffing scattered, two holes punched clean through the chair back. He studied it and pronounced it: darts of pure force. Somebody had been furious. But not at the keeper — those darts never miss their mark, Thorin pointed out, and the man bore no such marks. Somebody had aimed three bolts of force at a chair.

subject: Keeper's Chamber
fact: The Keeper's Chamber showed signs of a targeted, non-random intrusion. A silver pedestal, ebony pipe, and cherry tobacco were present — the latter used to mask poison odor. A metal safe stood open, containing four sealed sapphire pouches, a raven figurine, healing and water-breathing potions, diamonds, platinum, and gold — all untouched except for one missing sapphire and one missing spell parchment. A toppled marble statue of a hooded old man holding a candle lay near armchairs. A chair bore three puncture wounds from force darts, with no corresponding injuries on the body.
source_quote: Tobacco smoke would hide the smell of poison. Of course it would.

subject: Keeper's Chamber
fact: The chamber contained a desk with spellbooks, a safe with untouched treasure and one missing sapphire, a toppled statue of A'lai Aivenmore, an armchair with three force-dart impacts, a silver pedestal, an ebony pipe with cherry tobacco, and a tea table — all preserved in the state left by the killer.
source_quote: The room itself kept volunteering details.

subject: Keeper's chamber entry
fact: The safe’s door was open and undamaged — no forced entry — indicating the killer had either the combination or a key, or the safe was not locked.
source_quote: Zalthir checked the lock. Open, but undamaged. No forced entry. The killer had the combination, or had no need of one.

subject: Keeper's chamber safe
fact: The safe in the Keeper's chamber contained a king's ransom in gold, platinum, diamonds, and potions — but one sapphire and one spell parchment were missing, indicating targeted theft, not robbery.
source_quote: Still inside the safe were four sealed pouches, each with its sapphire — and beside them a figurine of a raven, a potion of supreme healing, another of water breathing, five diamonds each worth a fortune, a heap of platinum and gold, a small treasury left untouched. 'In other words, score what they left them.'

subject: Keeper's Desk
fact: The Keeper's Desk held blue ink, *The Discoveries*, *The Golden Ass*, and other writing materials, with the blue ink in *The Discoveries* being the most recent, indicating Janussi’s final intellectual activity before death.
source_quote: In the middle of the desk sat a spellbook. *The Discoveries.* Beside it, blue ink, fresh enough that it had a sequence to it. The blue ink on *The Discoveries* had been laid down after the blue ink on another book. *The Golden Ass.*

subject: Keeper's tower
fact: The Keeper's tower is referenced as the location of Hollypocket’s apartment below it, and the site of Janussi’s chamber and death.
source_quote: Hollypocket's apartment sat below the Keeper's tower

subject: Keeper's tower
fact: The Keeper's tower is the central location of the investigation, housing Janussi’s apartment below it, and serving as the site of all observed confrontations, the midnight thud, and the final moments of his life.
source_quote: Hollypocket's apartment sat below the Keeper's tower — modest, but with room to breathe…

subject: poison concealment method
fact: Tobacco smoke was used to mask the smell of poison in Janussi’s chamber.
source_quote: You don't fill a room with smoke to kill a man — you fill a room with smoke to keep him from smelling what's already there.

subject: silver pedestal and ebony pipe
fact: A silver pedestal and finely carved ebony pipe with cherry tobacco were found near the desk — the tobacco likely used to mask the scent of poison.
source_quote: A silver pedestal by the desk, an ebony pipe finely carved, cherry tobacco. Pretty, until Zalthir's instinct landed it — tobacco smoke would hide the smell of poison. Of course it would.

subject: the Tower
fact: The tower is the primary setting where Queenie observes events. It contains the armchamber, corridor, and stairways where key incidents — impersonation, theft, and murder — occurred.
source_quote: She had settled into Janussi's armchair for a nap... she retreated to the corridor... coming down the steps.

subject: Tower Chamber
fact: The tower chamber is the central location of the investigation. Queenie observed all key events here: the force attack, the book's removal, the impersonator’s appearance, and Daral’s exit. It is a space of surveillance and quiet dominance by the cat.
source_quote: she was napping in Janussi's armchair

subject: tower corridor
fact: Queenie retreated to the tower corridor upon seeing Daral’s action.
source_quote: she retreated to the corridor

subject: Underdark
fact: The Underdark is referenced by Zalthir as a place where violence is honest and six angles are run at once, contrasted with Candlekeep’s hidden grudges.
source_quote: In the Underdark everyone runs six angles at once and at least there it's honest about being a knife fight.

subject: Velkynvelve elevation
fact: Velkynvelve sits 100 feet above the cavern floor.
source_quote: Drow outpost was 100' in the sky

subject: chasme count
fact: Five years old, sleet-grey, and entirely uninterested — Queenie the cat is present.
source_quote: Queenie — five years old, sleet-grey, and entirely uninterested in being disturbed

subject: chasme count
fact: Four chasme demons are present in the cavern above the prisoners' tower.
source_quote: four chasme and two vrock

subject: Daral Yashenti's hostility count
fact: Daral Yashenti confronted Janussi twice in one day, shouting insults and fleeing the second encounter.
source_quote: Daral shouted at poor Janussi... 'You're not fit to be the candle keep's keeper'... he ran away so fast.

subject: Impersonator (Sylvira mimic)
fact: A figure wearing Sylvira Savikas's appearance but lacking her scent appeared in the tower after her initial attack. This indicates either shapeshifting, illusion, or a disguise worn by another individual — likely the true perpetrator.
source_quote: But she didn't smell like the demon lady, though.

subject: statue
fact: A marble statue, three feet tall, had fallen over — not awakened or animated — and was knocked down by A'lai Aivenmore in shock upon discovering the body; it posed no threat.
source_quote: The statue had simply fallen... Three feet of marble. Yes — a man could stagger into that and bring it down...

subject: the cat
fact: The cat, though not a combatant, provided information during the investigation — its behavior or knowledge was relevant enough for Fembris to mention it as a source, suggesting it may have witnessed or interacted with the killer or the missing items.
source_quote: after we'd talked to the cat — long story, the cat had things to say.

subject: the cat
fact: The five-year-old housecat was present in Janussi’s chamber at the time of death; Daz intends to use a Stonespeaker crystal to interrogate it for evidence — the only non-human witness with potential firsthand knowledge of the event.

subject: tiefling
fact: Sylvira Savikas is a tiefling — a creature with innate darkvision — whose use of a lantern contradicts her biological capabilities, making her actions suspicious and indicative of intent to obscure or reveal something to others.
source_quote: She's a tiefling, and she can see in the dark without any light at all.

subject: torn demon lady
fact: The torn demon lady came down the steps — Sylvira's shape, but not her scent.
source_quote: she'd prowled the nighttime cycle and seen the torn demon lady coming down the steps — Sylvira's shape

subject: unknown poison substance
fact: A black, unidentified substance found on Janussi’s fingertip, lower lip, and tongue could not be recognized by Glabbagool, an ooze that has ingested countless Underdark materials, indicating it is a rare or unnatural poison.
source_quote: When even a creature that has eaten the Underdark can't place a poison, you've learned the poison is worth being afraid of.

subject: A'lai Aivenmore
fact: A'lai Aivenmore, the Great Reader, discovered Janussi’s body at dawn and knocked over the statue in shock — his reaction was instinctive, not malicious.
source_quote: The Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore had knocked it over in shock when he found the body at dawn.

subject: Brother Tharusk
fact: Brother Tharusk is referenced as possibly the originator of the Garden Shadow’s saying about absence, described as the tall one who always smelled of incense.
source_quote: The Garden Shadow had a saying about that — or possibly Brother Tharusk did, the tall one who always smelled of incense

subject: Daral
fact: Daral is a man with a distinctive odor who carried away a book — later identified as *The Golden Ass* — from the scene. He activated a 'hypnotic block' (a book) that rendered him motionless and uninterested in scratching the cat, and exited the tower while Janussi was still alive.
source_quote: when I later saw him run downstairs with a hypnotic block.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral is a man with a distinctive odor who used a hypnotic block — later identified as the book *The Golden Ass* — to immobilize others. He exited the scene with the book and was present when Janussi was still alive.
source_quote: when I later saw him run downstairs with a hypnotic block.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral is described as the 'stinky breath one' by Queenie, and is the one who carried away The Golden Ass under his arm.
source_quote: there is a precision to how cats categorize people that I find I respect. No titles. No politics. Just the relevant data: gait, smell. ... and later Daral, *the stinky breath one*.

subject: Daral Yashenti
fact: Daral Yashenti is Janussi’s long-standing rival, publicly unimpressed by the sellswords, and now the prime suspect due to motive, opportunity, and the symbolic weight of his grudge — a decades-old grievance that has hardened into a weapon.
source_quote: He's the one who called you sellswords... He's the one who was very, you know, that not seemed, very impressed with you.

subject: Daral Yashenti
fact: Daral Yashenti is described as having shouted at Janussi, 'You're not fit to be the candle keep's keeper,' and called him 'nothing but a glorified book peddler,' and was heard pounding on Janussi’s door at half past ten, leading to a loud argument before fleeing.
source_quote: You're not fit to be the candle keep's keeper, Daral shouted at poor Janussi

subject: Daral Yashenti
fact: Daral Yashenti was Janussi’s long-standing rival, having engaged in at least two violent arguments with him on the day of the murder, including a drunken second confrontation; he called the investigators 'sellswords' dismissively; he is a prime suspect due to motive, opportunity, and hostile history.

subject: Daral Yashenti
fact: Daral Yashenti, nursing a hangover, verbally attacked Janussi twice — calling him unfit to be candle keeper and a 'glorified book peddler' — and later returned drunk, forcing entry and provoking another argument before Janussi fled upstairs.
source_quote: You're not fit to be the candle keep's keeper, Daral shouted at poor Janussi… nothing but a glorified book peddler…

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believed he could talk to the cat using the Stonespeaker crystal.
source_quote: I think I can talk to the cat,

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believes a corpse does not lie and that everything it knows is written on it, to be read by the observer.
source_quote: There is a particular comfort in a corpse. It does not lie. It does not run a counter-play. Everything it knows is written on it, and all I have to do is read.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believes information is currency, and so is scratching behind the ears.
source_quote: Information is currency. So, evidently, is scratching behind the ears.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believes the first rule is to read the witness who doesn't know what they're a witness to.
source_quote: The first rule is to read the witness who doesn't know what they're a witness to.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believes the killer rolled Janussi onto his back after death to remove his heart.
source_quote: And then the patient hands arriving after, in no hurry at all, rolling the body and opening the chest to make certain he stayed gone.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz intends to establish what the other party wants and provide exactly enough of it to keep the conversation his.
source_quote: I have run a few of those. Establish what the other party wants and provide exactly enough of it to keep the conversation yours.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is an investigator who showed disinterest during emotional testimony but reacted sharply to the lantern revelation — indicating prior knowledge or hidden involvement with Sylvira Savikas or the murder.
source_quote: Daz, I noticed, was paying the weeping woman no attention whatsoever… Hmm," said Daz, suddenly listening after all.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is an observant ally who connects disparate clues — the locket, the missing book, and the library keys — with sudden clarity, indicating he is synthesizing the investigation’s hidden patterns.
source_quote: So could that be the key to the library that was around there? Did somebody... that might explain why that stuff got deleted off the library, or off that book that no one should have touched.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the interrogator who questioned Queenie, pieced together the timeline, and recognized the significance of her observations. He is the one who connected the locket, the keys, the book, and the shapeshifter.
source_quote: I let the dots connect themselves out loud.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the one who says, 'I like the way you're thinking,' and later listens intently when Hollypocket describes Sylvira Savikas carrying a lantern, and is noted as paying no attention to her weeping.
source_quote: I like the way you're thinking,

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the cat had been in the chamber and believed it might provide an alibi or witness testimony.
source_quote: The animal had been in the chamber; the dead don't volunteer alibis, but a five-year-old housecat with opinions might.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz notices clotted blood under the nose and smeared bloodstains on the right sleeve of the tunic, indicating Janussi was writing when killed.
source_quote: Clotted blood under the nose. Smeared bloodstains on the right sleeve of the tunic — the *right* sleeve, the working hand.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz notices three circular impacts and holes in the armchair and identifies them as darts of pure force.
source_quote: Three circular impacts, horsehair stuffing scattered, two holes punched clean through the chair back.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz performed a meticulous forensic analysis of the body, identifying the tempo of the killer as deliberate and unhurried; he noted the black substance on Janussi’s finger and lip was not ink, but something darker and unknown; he reconstructed the sequence of death: poisoning, fall, desecration.
source_quote: The skill wasn't in identifying the substance. It was in knowing, with certainty, what it was not.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz possesses a Stonespeaker crystal and is capable of communicating with beasts; he remained detached during emotional testimony but became alert when Sylvira’s lantern and the glowing face were mentioned, indicating he suspects magical involvement.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realized the locket and the key to the Hightower Library were connected to the missing book and the deletion of records.
source_quote: So could that be the key to the library that was around there? Did somebody… that might explain why that stuff got deleted off the library, or off that book that no one should have touched.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realizes the black substance on Janussi’s finger and lip is not ink, because it is darker than the ink in the well.
source_quote: The tip of his left forefinger was blackened. Not blue. Darker than blue. And the same dark smudge sat dead-center on his lower lip. ... No. Not ink. That was the entire point of the long look — not that the finger was stained, but that the stain was *wrong*.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz refused to drink the herbal tea offered by Hollypocket.
source_quote: Thorin declined — "No thank you, I'm good."

subject: Daz
fact: Daz respects the precision with which cats categorize people.
source_quote: There is a precision to how cats categorize people that I find I respect.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz says, 'I'll give Queenie a little tickle,' and tickles her, acknowledging that information is currency and so is scratching behind the ears.
source_quote: "I'll give Queenie a little tickle," I said, and tickled. Information is currency. So, evidently, is scratching behind the ears.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz suddenly listened when Zalthir mentioned the lantern and Sylvira’s tiefling nature.
source_quote: Hmm," said Daz, suddenly listening after all.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz suspects the black substance is poison because of its unusual darkness and the way it was transferred from page to finger to lip.
source_quote: Do we think this black stuff might be poisonous? I thought it the likeliest answer.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz suspects the killer took only one sapphire and one parchment because they needed exactly that one thing, not because they were greedy.
source_quote: Somebody is trying to build a sapphire spell... a spell that requires a sapphire. ... Whoever did this came in, took one sapphire, and walked past a king's ransom.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz thinks the killer had time and was not in a rush, because the blows were precise and there was no blood spray.
source_quote: The blows had been precise. Too precise, too close together, for a man fighting back. No spray across the room — no blood pressure left to throw it. Janussi had been dead before his chest was opened. Whoever did this had not been in a rush. He had not been trying to kill. He had been desecrating a corpse at his leisure, with nowhere to be.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz understands that the chip in Janussi’s tooth came from falling face-first, not from the murder itself.
source_quote: He had fallen forward. Face-first. Chipped the tooth on the way down.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz was paying no attention to Hollypocket’s weeping, lost in his own thoughts.
source_quote: Daz, I noticed, was paying the weeping woman no attention whatsoever, off somewhere in his own ledger.

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris identifies Daral Yashenti as Janussi’s long-time rival and reveals that Janussi held one of the two keys to the Hightower Library, and that the other key is held by Kalan.
source_quote: Oh, that'll be Daral Yashenti. Those two have been at each other's throats for years.

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris is an assistant who, despite nervousness, becomes a key source of information, revealing Daral Yashenti as Janussi’s long-standing rival, the missing locket, and the existence of two Hightower Library keys, one held by Janussi and the other by Kalan.
source_quote: That'll be Daral Yashenti. Those two have been at each other's throats for years... Janussi held one of the two keys of the Hightower Library... the other key is heralded by the gate warden, Kalan.

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris provided the critical missing detail that Janussi held one of the keys to the Hightower Library, enabling the connection between the theft, deletion, and access.
source_quote: Janussi held one of the two keys to the Hightower Library.

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris supplies the missing detail that Janussi held one of the two keys to the Hightower Library.
source_quote: Fembris, *by golly*, supplied the column I was missing: Janussi held one of the two keys to the Hightower Library.

subject: Fheminor
fact: Fheminor is a short-legged individual who arrived at the tower in the evening, observed by Queenie as one of the first guests. No further details about their role in the events were provided.
source_quote: the short-legged one

subject: Fheminor
fact: Fheminor is described by Queenie as 'the short-legged one' and is the first evening guest to arrive.
source_quote: first Fheminor, *the short-legged one*, and later Daral, *the stinky breath one*.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum applied his healer’s expertise to determine the broken nose and bruising occurred before death; he identified the chain impression and broken lead links on Janussi’s neck as evidence of a locket forcibly removed; he ruled out robbery by noting the untouched treasury and only one sapphire stolen.
source_quote: The dead don't mark. The body has to be defending itself to make a bruise, and a corpse defends nothing.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes most things are funnier to him than they are to Zalthir.
source_quote: Most things, he does.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes the safe was not forced open because the lock was undamaged, meaning the killer had the combination or no need for it.
source_quote: The safe. A box of metal as wide as a man's reach, sunk into the tower wall, its door standing open. ... Open, but undamaged. No forced entry.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum correctly determined the nose was broken pre-mortem by analyzing bruising patterns, and later confirmed the wound was cleanly inflicted, suggesting a skilled assailant.
source_quote: His read of the wound came clean — sharp work this time — and the nose had broken before death.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum feels a quiet sorrow at the image of a clerk dying mid-sentence in his own library.
source_quote: I noted that and felt something I didn't examine too closely — a clerk dying mid-sentence in his own library. There are worse exits.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum feels relieved that someone else has taken an expense off his account.
source_quote: Well, that saves me money on potions," said Grygum, relieved — someone else had just taken an expense off his account.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum finds the idea of buying another adventure funnier than Zalthir does.
source_quote: He found this funnier than I did.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum heard Hollypocket describe Daral Yashenti as drunk and pounding on Janussi’s door at half past ten.
source_quote: Daral came back at half past ten, drunk as a skunk, pounding on the door until Janussi let him in

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum heard Hollypocket say Janussi ran away from Daral faster than she’d ever seen him run.
source_quote: I'd never seen him run away so fast.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum heard Hollypocket say she saw Sylvira Savikas’s face glowing red in the candlelight around 2 or 3 a.m.
source_quote: I swear I could see that devil woman's — Sylvira Savikas's — face glowing red in the candlelight.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum intended to ask the housekeeper, Hollypocket, what was missing or out of place.
source_quote: go find, say, the housekeeper, and ask her, what is missing or out of place.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is Thorin’s partner in inquiry, sharing a habit of overlapping speech and complementary investigative instincts; he prioritizes tangible evidence over political grudges and pushes for the housekeeper’s testimony to identify missing items.
source_quote: One thing we need is somebody who knows what should be here, so they can tell us if anything's missing.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is an assistant who noticed the locket was unasked and prompted Daz to inquire about it, recognizing its importance despite Queenie’s reluctance to describe it.
source_quote: Daz, why don't you ask the cat anyway? It's gonna be a weird description from a cat, but…

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is relieved that someone else has taken an expense off his account, saving him money on potions.
source_quote: Well, that saves me money on potions," said Grygum, relieved — someone else had just taken an expense off his account.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is the one who says, 'have any enemies, right?' and later proposes finding the housekeeper to determine what is missing or out of place.
source_quote: have any enemies, right?

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed that Hollypocket believed Janussi had incurred Sylvira’s wrath that morning.
source_quote: I was never sure but what the keeper saw in her, but he certainly incurred her wrath that morning.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum notices the impression of a chain on Janussi’s neck and identifies two broken lead links as evidence of a locket or necklace being torn off.
source_quote: The impression of a chain on the back and sides, and beneath it two broken lead links. Something had hung there, and someone had torn it off him.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum observed the blue ink sequence, recognized the shift from jokes to spell research in Janussi’s notes, and dismissed Thorin’s theories as amusing but unsupported — he found humor in the absurdity of the gift tag’s tone.
source_quote: Oh, the mystery... You have to go buy the other adventure. ... He found this funnier than I did.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum observes that the treasure in the safe was untouched, indicating the killer was not motivated by greed.
source_quote: Still inside the safe were four sealed pouches, each with its sapphire — and beside them a figurine of a raven, a potion of supreme healing, another of water breathing, five diamonds each worth a fortune, a heap of platinum and gold, a small treasury left untouched.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum realizes the broken nose happened before death, because the bruising was formed while blood was still moving.
source_quote: The bruising around the broken nose held its color, dark and settled, the way bruising only sits when blood was still moving when it formed.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum remembers that bruising cannot form on a corpse because there is no living tissue to swell.
source_quote: Bruising doesn't form on a corpse; there's no living tissue to swell.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum seeks concrete evidence of what is missing from the room — he pushes for the housekeeper’s testimony to establish baseline normalcy; he is pragmatic, focused on physical absence rather than motive, and is the one who directs the team to Hollypocket.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum suspects the tobacco pipe was used to mask the smell of poison.
source_quote: tobacco smoke would hide the smell of poison. Of course it would.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum thinks the statue of A'lai Aivenmore was knocked over accidentally by the scholar who discovered the body.
source_quote: The statue had simply fallen, it turned out. The Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore had knocked it over in shock when he found the body at dawn.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum understood that Sylvira was carrying a lantern she didn’t need because she could see in the dark.
source_quote: She was carrying a lantern. She's a tiefling, and she can see in the dark without any light at all.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum wanted to find someone who knew what should be in the room to identify what was missing.
source_quote: One thing we need is somebody who knows what should be here, so they can tell us if anything's missing.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum was found dead with blackened forefinger, center of lower lip, and tip of tongue — signs of licking ink from a poisoned book. He had a chipped front tooth and a broken nose with settled bruising, indicating an assault occurred before death. A chain impression on his neck bore broken lead links, suggesting a locket or necklace was torn from him. His death was not from the fall or poisoning alone, but from a deliberate heart extraction after a struggle.
source_quote: The dead don't mark. The body has to be defending itself to make a bruise, and a corpse defends nothing.

subject: Hollypocket
fact: Hollypocket is the elderly gnome caretaker of Janussi's apartment, who observed multiple heated arguments among the Great Readers before his death and provided key testimonies about their behavior and tensions.
source_quote: I do hate gossip, but if it's necessary for the investigation…

subject: Hollypocket
fact: Hollypocket reports overhearing violent arguments between Janussi and Kalan Strongbranch, Teles Ahvoste, Daral Yashenti, and Sylvira Savikas, and describes seeing Sylvira's face glowing red in candlelight at 2–3 a.m. while carrying a lantern.
source_quote: I was bringing the keeper his morning tea when I passed Kalan Strongbranch on the steps.

subject: Hollypocket
fact: Hollypocket, the housekeeper, observed Janussi's daily routines and the violent interactions with his colleagues; she heard a midnight thud and witnessed Sylvira Savikas carrying a lantern at 2–3 a.m., an act inconsistent with tiefling physiology, suggesting deliberate concealment.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi had been taking notes in blue ink at the time of his death, with fresh stains on his right sleeve — the working hand — and a chip in one front tooth from a forward fall.
source_quote: Clotted blood under the nose. Smeared bloodstains on the right sleeve of the tunic — the *right* sleeve, the working hand. And blotches of midnight blue across the cuff. I knew that blue. 'Wasn't the blue ink — the ink they used in the books?' It was. Janussi had been taking notes when this happened. Writing hand, fresh stains. A man interrupted at work. And a chip in one of his front teeth, the edge jagged. Recent.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi is a man who carried a locket at all times, held one of the two keys to the Hightower Library, and was the victim of a theft and murder. He had a romantic entanglement with Sylvira Savikas and was last seen alive after Daral departed with a book.
source_quote: He carried it all the time. He never took it off.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi is described as a scholar who kept his chamber thick with tobacco smoke to medicate his failing lungs, annotated a comedy book with both jokes and spell notes in blue ink, carried a locket always, and was the target of multiple violent arguments.
source_quote: Janussi had loved the stuff — kept his chamber thick with it, medicated his failing lungs with the smell of it, lived inside a haze on purpose.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was a Keeper of the Tome who was murdered after being struck in the face, falling forward and chipping a tooth, and then having his heart torn out and his ribcage smashed, with blackened finger and lip indicating he had been reading a poisoned page and wetting his fingertip on his lip.
source_quote: Janussi, Keeper of the Tome, was laid out before us, and the early findings were already on the table. The heart was gone — torn out, not for any wound it would cause, but as a guard against any working that calls the dead back to answer. The tip of his left forefinger was blackened. Not blue. Darker than blue. And the same dark smudge sat dead-center on his lower lip.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was a man who carried a locket at all times, held one of two keys to the Hightower Library, and was killed after a confrontation with Sylvira Savikas. He was last seen alive when Daral exited with a book.
source_quote: He carried it all the time. He never took it off.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was a scholar who annotated a comedy book with obscure spell notes and jokes using the same fresh ink, indicating deliberate dual-layered cipher work; he wore a locket always, never removed it; he was addicted to tobacco smoke to mask his failing lungs; he was murdered, likely by poison, with the smell hidden by smoke.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was struck in the face, returned to his desk, wrote notes in blue ink on *The Discoveries* and *The Golden Ass*, and was then killed — his heart and one sapphire and a locket removed, his nose broken, and his body rolled over.
source_quote: He'd been struck in the face, returned here, and written. Then he'd died.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was the victim, a scholar who held one-on-one meetings with the Great Readers before Deadwinter Day, carried a locket at all times, and was known to be polite but stiff, last seen alive fleeing upstairs after a violent confrontation with Daral Yashenti.
source_quote: He was such a nice man! A little stiff, maybe, but such a nice man!… He carried it all.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi’s tongue was blackened at the tip, confirming ingestion of the black substance, and his nose was broken before death, as bruising cannot form on a corpse.
source_quote: The tongue, blackened at the tip — ingestion confirmed twice over now. And a chip in one of his front teeth, the edge jagged. Recent. Not an old break worn smooth, but a fresh wound. The bruising around the broken nose held its color, dark and settled, the way bruising only sits when blood was still moving when it formed. subject: the black substance

source_quote: Darkness than blue. That was the entire point of the long look — not that the finger was stained, but that the stain was *wrong*. Darker than anything in his inkwell. Zalthir, ever the auditor of other people's competence, pushed on it — *our great detective took his long, careful look and still can't tell us if it's ink?* No. That was exactly what I could tell. The skill wasn't in identifying the substance. It was in knowing, with certainty, what it was *not*. Would't Glabbagool have ingested, like, all sorts of different kinds of materials and poisons and goo in the Underdark? We gave him the substance. He gave it his best.
